metadata.title: Pagination — LFI `meta` to TPP `Links`
metadata.description: How page-based pagination flows from the LFI's Ozone Connect response through the API Hub, converted into the Links envelope consumed by the TPP.

intro.text: This article uses GET /accounts/{accountId}/transactions as the worked example. The same behaviour applies to GET /accounts/{accountId}/statements — and to any other endpoint where the LFI chooses to paginate.

blocks.text: The Hub issues one page-based request per TPP call:

page is 1-indexed; page-size defaults to 100. Filtering parameters ( fromBookingDateTime, toBookingDateTime ) are applied before pagination — totalRecords and totalPages reflect the filtered result set, not the whole table.
The LFI returns the slice for the requested page, plus a meta block describing the full filtered result set:

rows: true if the response is a page of a larger result set. false or omitted if the LFI returned the full result set in a single response
ceil(totalRecords / page-size) — the last page number the Hub may request
The total number of records in the filtered result set across all pages

blocks.text: The LFI MUST return records in a deterministic order so pagination is stable across successive page requests.
The TPP does not send page or page-size. Pagination is expressed through the Hub's URL parameters on the Links returned in the previous response.
The Hub converts the LFI's meta into Meta and Links:
The Hub derives each link from the LFI's meta.totalPages and the current page:

rows: The URL that produced this response
Current URL with page = currentPage - 1. Omitted on the first page
Current URL with page = currentPage + 1. Omitted on the last page

subsections.heading: When the LFI returns an unpaginated response

blocks.text: If the LFI returns meta.paginated: false (or omits paginated ), the full result set is in a single response. The Hub emits Meta.TotalPages: 1, a Links.Self, and no First / Prev / Next / Last.

sections.heading: A filtered query that yields nothing

blocks.text: The Hub propagates this as an empty Data array with Meta.TotalPages: 0. 404 MUST NOT be returned.

sections.heading: Forward-compatibility on the TPP side, simplicity on the LFI side

blocks.text: The TPP standards follow UK Open Banking conventions — opaque Links let the Hub evolve its pagination strategy (cursor-based, time-sliced, etc.) without breaking TPP clients. The LFI side is deliberately simpler: page/page-size is the lowest-common-denominator interface that every core banking system can serve cheaply. The Hub absorbs the translation.
GET /accounts/{accountId}/statements works identically: the LFI paginates by page / page-size and returns meta.totalPages / meta.totalRecords; the Hub emits Links and Meta.TotalPages on the TPP side.

Other list endpoints ( /beneficiaries, /direct-debits, /scheduled-payments, /standing-orders, /products, /accounts/{accountId}/customer ) may pursue the same model if the LFI chooses to paginate them, but the expectation is that the full result set is returned in a single response.
